text:
alex: FYI -- after the eu-west fractional-consolidation we started seeing short, sharp p99 spikes on inference traffic from multiple tenants around 21:45 UTC. Looks like egress contention, not GPU.
maria: yep, noticed the same. TCP retransmits bumped, kernel tx_queue depth spiking on a subset of ToRs.
kevin: do we have a map of tenant -> SNAT/ToR mapping? wondering if consolidation shuffled previously-separated egress onto the same ToR.
alex: pulling. early signal shows ~6 hot-tenants ended up behind the same ToR SNAT pair (toR-12).
sara: infra-bot shows fractional-consolidate-v2 ran at 21:30 and packed hot-shelf slots tighter. infra-bot: policy-run(rc=rc-20260320-19) completed :white_check_mark:
infra-bot: current-snats: toR-12=[snat-a,snat-b], toR-13=[snat-c] ; affected-tenants=[t-12,t-42,t-77,t-99,t-108,t-204]
ops-lead: hypothesis: packing changed network egress adjacency -> ToR head-of-line + switch burst coalescing -> p99 tails.
maria: agree. this is classic cross-tenant egress coupling. short-term: try splitting SNAT set across two ToRs for the hot tenants (soft split) to smooth microbursts.
kevin: propose a non-invasive canary: 15% of flows for label=hot-infer use backup SNAT on toR-13. If p99 drops we expand. Command to run:
```bash
redwoodctl network redirect-egress --region eu-west --selector 'label=hot-infer' --percent 15 --from-snat toR-12 --to-snat toR-13 --reason "egress-stitch-canary"
```
kevin: I'll also enable tcp_queue probes and a per-snat p99 tail metric.
alex: instead of full rollback this buys time and avoids capacity churn. good call.
sara: smoke harness must run after 15% goes live. I'll kick it off and report SLA deltas.
maria: can we also monitor BGP path churn on the leafs? if ECMP shifts we might see uneven distribution.
kevin: will add bfd/bgp delta probe.
infra-bot: redirect-egress initiated (id=rj-20260320-nw1), status=rolling
kevin: canary live @ 21:55. starting 5m burn.
ops-lead: reminder: mute high-frequency paging for p99 alerts for 10m to avoid noise.
alex: confirmed.
sara: smoke results after 10m: no SLA breach, p95 stable, p99 on previously affected racks dropped ~50%.
maria: good signal. keep canary 20m more then go to 50%.
kevin: expanding to 50% now. command: ```bash
redwoodctl network redirect-egress --id rj-20260320-nw1 --percent 50
```
kevin: metrics story: tcp_queue median unchanged, tail improved on toR-12, toR-13 tcp_queue increased slightly but under threshold.
ops-lead: cautious: watch egress-cost delta for cross-az egress if we start routing across different uplinks. Cost impact should be negligible inside same AZ but flag if it climbs.
maria: long-term fix proposal: allocator should consider egress-affinity as a soft constraint when packing hot tenants. open to suggestions.
alex: +1. we should add an egress-vector to the placement score so we prefer to distribute tenants with heavy egress.
kevin: we can add a lightweight feature-flag: placement.score.weight.egress_affinity default 0.1 and run in experiment mode.
sara: ops check: update runbook infra/egress-mitigation with the canary commands, probes to run, and rollback criteria.
ops-lead: assign follow-ups: kevin -> instrument per-snat tails and BGP probes, run placement experiment; alex -> tenant->ToR correlation and historical pack delta; maria -> cost check and alert tuning; sara -> update runbook + smoke harness.
alex: timeline: will reconvene in 24h or earlier if signals reappear. thanks team. :thumbsup:
